QF.id: XIII Trading, Clearing, Settlement and Risk Management_72

question.text: For a cash-settled GOI bond futures contract, the Final Settlement Price (FSP) is the weighted average price of the underlying bond from trades on NDS-OM during the last two hours of the trading day, subject to a minimum of 5 trades. Suppose the prints in the last two hours on the expiry day are: Rs 101.50 for face value Rs 200 crore, Rs 102.00 for Rs 300 crore and Rs 101.00 for Rs 500 crore. What is the FSP?

answer.text: Rs 101.50 (simple average of the three traded prices)
Rs 102.00 (only the highest traded price in the window is used)

explanation.text: The Logic: Weighted average = (101.50 x 200 + 102.00 x 300 + 101.00 x 500) / (200 + 300 + 500) = (20,300 + 30,600 + 50,500) / 1,000 = 1,01,400 / 1,000 = Rs 101.40. The volume weighting gives more weight to the Rs 500 crore print at Rs 101.00, pulling the average below the simple mean. The Trap: A simple average of the three prints is (101.50 + 102.00 + 101.00) / 3 = Rs 101.50, not Rs 101.40 — using the simple average ignores the workbook's volume-weighting rule. Using only the highest price (Rs 102.00) or a single-day price ignores the multi-trade weighted-average requirement. Note: The minimum-5-trades condition exists to prevent thin trading from determining FSP. If fewer than 5 trades occur in the two-hour window, the FIMMDA / FBIL price for the bond is used as the fallback.
